candidates.title: Time for a digital divorce? Trade war puts spotlight on Canada's relationship with U.S. big tech
candidates.description: Tensions between Canada and the United States have raised concerns about Canada's digital sovereignty, but what does that term mean, and how can Canada promote it? Experts say it's about making sure Canada has tech alternatives and can effectively regulate all things digital, but that can prove difficult.

candidates.title: Bears, caribou and other animals are messing with this researcher's equipment, and he's got photos to prove it
candidates.description: Lucas Brehaut was hoping there’d be a lot of interest in his research, though it might be a case of “be careful what you wish for.” Caribou, moose, black bears, wolves, rabbits and owls have been messing with his research equipment.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Canada is everyone, for everyone': Carney meets with Alberta remain campaigners

candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.description: On a day when the compassion of people in Gander, N.L. was being celebrated, a chance encounter at a chicken restaurant led to a tour bus of Americans repaying the favour.

candidates.title: Drone-powered ad for PC Health chatbot slammed as 'dystopian' by some residents
candidates.description: On Thursday night, more than a thousand drones lit up the sky above Toronto's waterfront displaying a list of health-related questions in what turned out to be an ad campaign for a new President's Choice AI-powered chatbot.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta government launches ad campaign on referendum questions
candidates.description: The Alberta government has launched a $4-million advertising campaign outlining its position on the 10 questions in the Oct. 19 referendum.

candidates.description: CBC News readers, viewers and listeners have been sending in questions about the trade war, often asking how Canada can turn up the heat on the U.S.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.description: Federal parole board documents show the 27-year-old man charged in a stabbing inside an Edmonton Sikh temple last month had a history of “serious and impulsive” violence, often driven by delusions, paranoia and conspiracy theories.

candidates.title: Would a $20 minimum wage in Quebec actually be a 'big blow' to the economy?
candidates.description: Québec Solidaire is pitching a $20 minimum wage to help bring relief to low-income workers, but Coalition Avenir Québec Leader Christine Fréchette said hiking the rate too quickly would have a detrimental ripple effect. Others aren't so sure.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Where I was on 9/11: Four people in N.L. share their stories
candidates.description: For many, Sept. 11, 2001, is a day they will never forget, and on the 25th anniversary of the attacks, four Newfoundlanders and Labradorians remember how they helped those in need.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Wildfires, permafrost thaw in Canada causing even more climate change, new study shows
candidates.description: These climate feedback loops, where climate change triggers more greenhouse gas emissions that in turn feed into even more climate change, could add 20 to 30 per cent more warming over current estimates for this century.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: As Dean Penney gets life sentence, sister says she's 'lost' without Jennifer Hillier-Penney

candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.description: Canada's Army formally made one of the biggest changes to its structure in decades Thursday by shifting from divisions based on geography to ones built around specific purposes. A new division, that prepares the army to rapidly deploy, will be headquartered in Edmonton.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Homelessness on the rise in Ontario while province on track to spend less, report says
candidates.description: Homelessness in Ontario is on the rise, climbing by more than 23 per cent over the past four years to more than 76,000 people, but the province is projected to spend less on it, the fiscal watchdog says in a new report.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.description: The Ontario Science Centre has laid off 31 workers, according to the union representing them. The union said the layoffs eliminated the centre's "standalone science unit."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cat in the Hat suspect who chased a teen girl in B.C. appears to be a trend copycat
candidates.description: A disturbing incident in which someone dressed in a Cat in the Hat costume chased a teenager in West Kelowna, B.C., occurred amid an online trend that twists the popular children's character into something sinister, leading police in some jurisdictions to warn of offline consequences.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Your guide to the U.S. midterms, and why they're crucial for Donald Trump
candidates.description: Here's everything you need to know about the upcoming U.S. midterm elections and why they're potentially crucial to how U.S. President Donald Trump wields power in his final two years in the White House.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iraq scrambles to address fallout from alleged militia attack on Saudi oil pipeline

candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump's call for united Ireland draws swift rejection from pro-British unionists
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he would "love" to see British-run Northern Ireland unify with Ireland, remarks made during a visit to Dublin that drew a sharp response from pro-British unionists in Northern Ireland.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.author: CBC News

Last month, the lab announced it made its first identification of previously unknown remains using a breakthrough technique.

candidates.title: Man accused in Mexican condo scheme claims he was a victim, too

But whatever you call it — a difference of opinion? an incongruity? the unpleasantness? — it's been going for more than 19 months. And it seems now that it could be several more months before hostilities are reduced, let alone ceased.
